title: Memories surviving metamorphosis are remapped to stay salient in the new body

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Memories surviving metamorphosis are remapped to stay salient in the new body

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In insects whose memories survive metamorphosis (caterpillar to butterfly), recall does not carry over specific caterpillar memories but generalizes and remaps them (e.g. from leaves to food) so that the learned relationship keeps its salience in the new body and environment.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 3. Remapping Memories: Beyond Storage and Simple Modification

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The process of memory and recall not only functionally generalizes (abstracts20) the information (not leaves, but “food”), but most importantly, remaps21 it in a way that the basic relationship learned maintains its salience in a new body and environment.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “3. Remapping Memories: Beyond Storage and Simple Modification”. Scope: Holometabolous insects (e.g. Lepidoptera) retaining learned associations through metamorphosis

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Retention and generalization have measurable behavioural readouts, but the stronger claim that memories are remapped specifically to preserve salience needs controls rarely present in legacy experiments. Existing studies can resolve only a restricted version.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyse individual insect conditioning and post-metamorphic choice data to test whether retained responses transfer from the trained cue or resource to novel cues serving the same functional category. Category-level transfer without cue-specific retention supports remapping; strictly cue-specific retention refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Post-metamorphic preference can reflect innate attraction or relearning.

Classic studies may report only aggregate results.

Food salience is inferred rather than directly observed.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Retention of a learned association through metamorphosis is a published, quantitative behavioral result, and that result can speak to whether specific memories survive. The further claim that recall generalizes and remaps, illustrated as leaves becoming food, is not what those assays measured, and the scores are not in a reusable dataset. Existing papers can test part of the statement and leave the remapping clause open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Train a specific cue-outcome association in a caterpillar, then after metamorphosis test that same cue against a generalized food cue and against novel cues. Survival of only a generalized mapping would support the claim; retained response to the specific trained cue would refute the claim that specific caterpillar memories do not carry over.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Very few holometabolous species have been tested through metamorphosis.

The main open behavioral study is odor-shock retention in Manduca, not a leaves-to-food remapping test.

Trial-level choices are in the paper, not a public behavioral repository.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.45
